instruction.text: Label the areas of the Maya city.

hint.label: Ceremonial centre
hint.text: The ceremonial centre of Maya cities is where all the temples were.

feedback.finish: The royals and nobles lived in the ceremonial centre of the city. The temples and palaces in the centre took many years to be built because they were intricately decorated.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The buildings in the centre of Maya cities were often made out of limestone because it was easy to find across Mesoamerica.
Other materials, like volcanic rock and sandstone, were also used when limestone wasn’t available.

atoms.a: What were most ceremonial buildings made out of?
Which two other materials were used when limestone wasn’t available?

feedback.finish: The Maya managed to create all of these impressive buildings without inventing the wheel! This means they had to carry a lot of rocks themselves and push heavier ones along on logs.

instruction.text: What is this traditional Maya house made out of?

feedback.finish: Ordinary Maya homes were built in an oval shape with wooden poles.

instruction.text: Drag the mud to the wooden poles.

feedback.finish: To build a house, the Maya would put the poles in the ground and then cover them in clay and mud. This is a building technique called wattle and daub.

instruction.text: Select the roof of the Maya house.

feedback.finish: The roofs of Maya houses were thatched. This means that they were made of plants or straw.

atoms.b: Most traditional Maya houses only had ((++one five)) room.
One half of the room was used for ((++sleeping running)) at night, and the other was for daytime activities.
Beds were made out of ((++tree_branches glass)) with mats placed on top.
Extra ((++houses beds)) may also have been built for cooking and storage.
